subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: After fixing authorization ordering, should plugin-runtime callers remain fail-closed on every legacy ownerless session row, or should OpenClaw provide an explicit ownership migration or adoption path?
rationale: The PR changes access to persisted rows created before ownership metadata existed, and repository source establishes the mechanics but not the intended upgrade and security policy.

options.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
options.body: Require persisted ownership to match the authenticated plugin and leave operator or non-plugin clients as the recovery path.

options.title: Add explicit ownership migration
options.body: Provide a doctor or owner-approved migration that assigns legacy rows before plugin-runtime patch access is allowed.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Require persisted ownership to match the authenticated plugin and leave operator or non-plugin clients as the recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: The session accessor, patch-projection, and plugin-session lifecycle contracts trace primarily to this contributor's merged work.
